notes_for_owner: Written from formrig 0.13.2 (main 912c356, CI green on 2026-11-17). Contract mode: ./formrig install runs setup/install_all (the engine venv, the Rust engine module frg_engine built with maturin, the frontend), install-desktop installs PyInstaller and the desktop requirements, and desktop build passes --config FILE on to tauri build after building the frontend and freezing the engine; formrig.bat has the same three commands under cmd and its desktop build forwards every argument. The Rust toolchain is pinned to 1.99.1 by rust-toolchain.toml, which rustup honours on every runner. The engine is native code, so every platform builds on its own runner (no macos-x64=cross). On macOS the engine is a PyInstaller one-folder copied to src-tauri/engine and shipped as Resources/engine by src-tauri/tauri.macos.conf.json; with APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY set, setup/freeze_backend signs every Mach-O in it with hardened runtime, a timestamp and src-tauri/entitlements.plist, so notarization should pass; the first notarized build is the test. On Windows and Linux it is the one-file sidecar src-tauri/binaries/formrig-engine-<triple>. Linux packages are the list the app's own release-build.yml installed. No Tauri updater plugin and createUpdaterArtifacts false, so updater.tauri is false. Skills are .claude/skills (formrig-harness, formrig-rigging); the app has an MCP server (./formrig mcp). Catalogue: id, name, kind and summary follow formai.studio's catalog/products.json; identifier, .frig and .frgreturn come from tauri.conf.json; macOS 12 is its minimumSystemVersion. The app's old .github/workflows/release-build.yml still exists; formcompiler is the only builder, so the owner may remove it. Before the first run, give the read token access to nodemode-dev/formrig.
